Clairaut’s equation.

DEFINITION. Differential equation
                                        y = xy ′ + ϕ(y ′)                                     (13)

is called Clairaut’s equation.
Lagrange’s equation.

DEFINITION. Differential equation

                               A(y ′)y + B(y ′)x + C(y ′) = 0                               (14)

is called Lagrange’s equation.
Supposing that A(y ′) ̸= 0, we divide by it and thus (14) reads

                                      y = ϕ(y ′)x + ψ(y ′).                                   (15)

Sometimes DE (15) is called Lagrange’s equation. We see that, in fact, Lagrange’s equation is a
generalization of Clairaut’s equation (ϕ(y ′) = y ′). The method of solving first-order DE which resolved
with respect to y is the following: we use the change y ′(x) = p(x).
